nodes.name: Restriction of $\tilde\theta_*$ to the bottom cell
nodes.statement: The restriction of $\tilde{\theta}_* : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]$ along the morphism $KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) [-2] \hookrightarrow KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$, induced by the inclusion of the bottom cell $S^{-2} \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1}$ is the morphism \[ KU_*(U) \circ \sigma[-2] : KU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) [-2] \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]. \]
nodes.statement_short: On the bottom cell, $\tilde\theta_*$ restricts to $KU_*(U)\circ\sigma[-2]$.
nodes.label: lem:restrict_Theta

nodes.name: Power series form of $\tilde\theta_*$
nodes.statement: This result corresponds to the fact that the morphism $\tilde{\theta}_*$ is determined by the power series \[ \frac{1}{S} \left(\frac{1}{\log^{KU}T} - \frac{1}{T}\right) + \tilde{\theta} ' (S,T) \] where $\tilde{\theta}'$ is the formal power series introduced in Notation \ref{nota:tilde_theta_prime}.

nodes.name: Formula for $_{MU_*}K_{KU_*}$
nodes.statement: The morphism $$_{MU_*}K_{KU_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4])$$ is determined by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{S}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(S)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^{MU} T } - \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(T)} \Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: $_{MU_*}K_{KU_*}$: $(1/S-1/\underline b'(S))(1/\log^{MU}T-1/\underline b'(T))$.
nodes.label: prop:calculate_K_KU

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.14
nodes.statement: By construction $\underline{b}'$ corresponds to the image of $\underline{b}$ under the morphism induced by $MU_*MU \rightarrow MU_*KU$, and $\log^L$ maps to $\log^{MU}$. The result follows from Proposition \ref{prop:calculate_Xi}.
nodes.statement_short: Push Proposition 4.8 along $MU_*MU\to MU_*KU$.

nodes.name: Morphism $\tilde{\theta}'_*$
nodes.statement: Write $\tilde{\theta}'_*$ for the  morphism of $MU_*$-modules $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]$ determined by  $\tilde{\theta}'$.

nodes.name: Relation of $MU_*(\theta)\circ\sigma'$ and $K$
nodes.statement: There is an identification of morphisms in $\mathrm{Hom}_{MU_*} (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), MU_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4])$: \[ MU_* (\theta) \circ \sigma' = -\ _{MU_*}K_{KU_*} + (MU_*MU \otimes \tilde{\theta}'_*) \circ \psi_{MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)}. \]
conclusions:
MU_* (\theta) \circ \sigma'
	=
	-\  _{MU_*}K_{KU_*} + (MU_*MU \otimes \tilde{\theta}'_*) \circ \psi_{MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)}.
nodes.statement_short: $MU_*(\theta)\circ\sigma'=-{}_{MU_*}K_{KU_*}+(1\otimes\tilde\theta'_*)\circ\psi$.
nodes.label: cor:relate_MUtheta

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4.15
nodes.statement: Compare the calculation in Proposition \ref{prop:MUtheta_sigmap} with Proposition \ref{prop:calculate_K_KU}. (Note that the sign arises from the conventions used in defining the cobar complex, as in Proposition \ref{prop:cocycle-canonical-splitting}.)
nodes.statement_short: Compare Proposition 3.17 with Proposition 4.14.

nodes.name: Comodule primitives $\mathbf{P} M$
nodes.statement: For $M$ a left $MU_*MU$-comodule, write $\mathbf{P} M$ for the graded abelian group of comodule primitives.

nodes.name: Eilenberg-MacLane spectra $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}$, $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.statement: As above $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}$ denotes the rational Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum; its integral counterpart is denoted ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$.

nodes.name: Primitives and ordinary homology
nodes.statement: For $X$ a spectrum, there is a natural commutative diagram of graded abelian groups, induced by the orientation of ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$ and rationalization \[ \xymatrix{ \mathbf{P} MU_* X \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[d] & MU_* X \ar[r] & \mathbb{Z} \otimes_{MU_* } MU_* (X) \ar[r] & {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* X \ar[d] \\ \mathbf{P} MU_* X \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[rrr]_\cong &&& \mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}_* X, } \] in which the lower horizontal morphism is an isomorphism. If $MU_* X$ has no additive torsion, then $\mathbf{P} MU_* X \rightarrow {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* X$ is a monomorphism.
conclusions: $\mathbf{P} MU_* X \rightarrow {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* X$ is a monomorphism
nodes.statement_short: Primitives map to $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}_*X$, rationally isomorphically onto $\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Q}_*X$; injective if $MU_*X$ is torsion free.
nodes.label: lem:thom_orientation_primitives

nodes.name: Primitives of $MU_*((\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d})$
nodes.statement: Let $d$ be a natural number. Then $$ \mathbf{P} MU_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d}) \hookrightarrow {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d}) $$ is a morphism of algebras, where the product is induced by the $H$-space structure of $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty$. The homology ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d})$ is the free divided power algebra $\Gamma^* (\mathbb{Z}^{\oplus d}) $, hence $ \mathbf{P} MU_* ((\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)^{\wedge d})$ is a subalgebra of $\Gamma^* (\mathbb{Z}^{\oplus d}) $.
nodes.label: exam:prim_CP

nodes.name: Primitive generators $p_n$
nodes.statement:
The primitives $ \mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ were calculated by David Segal
\cite{segal}; an elegant approach is given by Miller in \cite[Proposition 4.1]{miller}, where
the primitive generators $p_n \in MU_{2n}(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ are defined by means of the expansion
\[
\underline{\beta}_0(\exp (T))
=
\sum
\frac{p_n}{n!}T^n
\]
in $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$, so that $|p_n|= 2n$.
nodes.statement_short: $p_n$ defined by $\underline\beta_0(\exp T)=\sum p_nT^n/n!$.

nodes.name: Image of $p_n$ in ordinary homology
nodes.statement:
The morphism
$
\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow {\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)
$
sends $p_n$ to $ (\beta_1^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}})^n  = n! \beta_n^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$, where  the $\beta_i^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$ denote the canonical module generators of ${\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ (cf. \cite[Remark 4.2]{miller}).
nodes.statement_short: $p_n\mapsto(\beta_1^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}})^n=n!\beta_n^{\mathbf{H}\mathbb{Z}}$.

nodes.name: $p_i \otimes p_j$ are primitive
nodes.statement: By the Künneth isomorphism $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \cong MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$, for pairs of natural numbers $(i,j)$, $p_i \otimes p_j$ is a primitive of $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$.

nodes.name: Integral primitives of $MU_*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$
nodes.statement: The integral calculation of $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$   is an interesting and difficult problem: the elements $p_i \otimes p_j$ do not generate the primitives, due to delicate divisibility questions (cf. \cite{knapp_habilit}, \cite{baker_transfer} and \cite{BCRS}, for example).
nodes.statement_short: Compute the integral primitives of $MU_*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$; the $p_i\otimes p_j$ do not generate.

nodes.name: Rational basis of primitives
nodes.statement: The primitive $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ subgroup is a graded free $\mathbb{Z}$-module such that $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ has basis $\{ p_i \otimes p_j | i, j \geq 0 \}$.
conclusions:
graded free
$\mathbb{Z}$-module

$\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ has
basis $\{ p_i \otimes p_j | i, j \geq 0 \}$
nodes.label: lem:identify-primitives

nodes.name: Generating series $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{p} (S, T) $ denote the two-variable power-series in $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 ) \otimes \mathbb{Q} [[S, T]]$: \[ \mathfrak{p}(S, T):= \sum_{m,n \geq 0} p_m \otimes p_n \frac{S^m T^n}{m! n !}. \]
nodes.label: nota:primel

nodes.name: Generating series of primitives
nodes.statement: There is an identity of formal power series: \[ \mathfrak{p}(S, T) = \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp T). \]
conclusions: \mathfrak{p}(S, T) = \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp S) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (\exp T).
nodes.label: lem:identify_primel

nodes.name: Restriction of the double transfer to a primitive
nodes.statement:
A primitive $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree $2k$ in $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ corresponds to
a morphism of comodules
\[
\mathfrak{p} \in
\mathrm{Hom}_{MU_* MU}(MU_* [2k] , MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)).
\]
This induces a class $\mathfrak{p}^* [\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{MU_*MU} (MU_* [2k] , MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-4])$ and, by the chromatic connecting morphism $\partial_1$, the image of the double algebraic transfer:
\[
\mathfrak{p} ^* [e_\tau^2] = \partial_1 \mathfrak{p}^*  [\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^2 _{MU_*MU} (MU_*[2k] , MU_* [-4]),
\]
where the identification follows from Proposition \ref{prop:kappa-transfer}.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives
nodes.statement_short: A primitive $\mathfrak p$ gives $\mathfrak p^*[e_\tau^2]=\partial_1\mathfrak p^*[\kappa]$.

nodes.name: Cocycle $\kappa\circ\mathfrak{p}$ via $K\circ\mathfrak{p}$
nodes.statement:
By Proposition \ref{prop:calculate_Xi},  the cocycle $\kappa\circ \mathfrak{p}$ fits
into the commutative diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
MU_* [2k]
\ar[r]^(.4){K \circ \mathfrak{p}}
\ar[rd]_{\kappa \circ \mathfrak{p}}
&
MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]
\ar@{->>}[d]
\\
&
MU_* MU \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}} [-4].
}
\]
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives

nodes.name: Reduced Bernoulli numbers $\overline{B}_n^L, \overline{B}_n^R$
nodes.statement: Write $\overline{B}_n ^L, \overline{B}_n^R \in MU_*MU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ for the reduced Bernoulli numbers associated to the left (respectively right) $MU_*$-algebra structures.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives

nodes.name: $K$ on primitives
nodes.statement: The restriction of the morphism $K : MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \rightarrow MU_*MU\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]$ to the primitive elements is determined by \[ K (p_m \otimes p_n) = (\overline{B}^R_{m+1} - \overline{B}^L _{m+1})\overline{B}^R_{n+1} \] for natural numbers $m,n$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives
nodes.statement_short: $K(p_m\otimes p_n)=(\overline B^R_{m+1}-\overline B^L_{m+1})\overline B^R_{n+1}$.
nodes.label: prop:restrict_Xi_prim

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5.8
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:calculate_Xi}, the morphism $K $ is given by \[ \underline{\beta}_0 (x) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (y) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{x}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(x)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^L y } - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(y)} \Big). \] Lemma \ref{lem:identify_primel} identifies the generating formal power series $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ for the primitive elements $p_i \otimes p_j$; thus the image of $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ is given by substituting the power series $x= \exp^L S $, $y=\exp^L T$ in the above exression (note that the left module structure of $MU_*MU$ is used), which gives \[ \mathfrak{p}(S,T) \mapsto \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^L S}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(\exp^L S)} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\log^L ( \exp^L T)} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}(\exp^L T)} \Big). \] Simplifying and reversing the order in the two brackets, this gives: \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^R S}- \frac{1}{\exp^L S} \Big) \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^R T} - \frac{1}{T} \Big). \] The result follows from the definition of $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ and of the reduced Bernoulli numbers.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $x=\exp^LS$, $y=\exp^LT$ in the formula for $K$ and read off reduced Bernoulli numbers.

nodes.name: Formula for K
nodes.statement:
By Proposition \ref{prop:calculate_Xi}, the morphism $K $ is given by
\[
\underline{\beta}_0 (x) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (y)
\mapsto
\Big(
\frac{1}{x}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(x)}
\Big)
\Big(
\frac{1}{\log^L y }
- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(y)}
\Big).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Recall the formula for $K$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives

nodes.name: Substitution
nodes.statement:
Lemma \ref{lem:identify_primel} identifies the generating formal power series  $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ for the primitive elements $p_i \otimes p_j$; thus the image of $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ is given by substituting the power series $x= \exp^L
S $, $y=\exp^L T$ in the above exression (note that  the left module structure of $MU_*MU$ is used), which gives
\[
\mathfrak{p}(S,T)
\mapsto
\Big(
\frac{1}{\exp^L S}- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(\exp^L S)}
\Big)
\Big(
\frac{1}{\log^L ( \exp^L T)}
- \frac{1}{\underline{b}(\exp^L T)}
\Big).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $x=\exp^LS$, $y=\exp^LT$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives

nodes.name: Simplify
nodes.statement:
Simplifying and reversing the order in the two brackets, this gives:
\[
\Big(
\frac{1}{\exp^R S}- \frac{1}{\exp^L S}
\Big)
\Big(
\frac{1}{\exp^R T}
-
\frac{1}{T}
\Big).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Simplify using $\underline b=\exp^R\circ\log^L$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The result follows from the definition of $\mathfrak{p}(S,T)$ and  of the reduced Bernoulli numbers.
nodes.statement_short: Read off reduced Bernoulli numbers.
nodes.section: 5.2 Restricting the double transfer to primitives

nodes.name: Ring of holomorphic modular forms ${MF}$
nodes.statement:
Consider the ring ${MF}$ of
holomorphic forms of level one over the ring ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$, so that ${MF} \cong {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [c_4, c_6]$,
graded by weight.

nodes.name: $q$-expansion
nodes.statement:
The Fourier expansion at the cusp at infinity defines the
$q$-expansion ${MF}\hookrightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]] [u]$, a
monomorphism of rings by the $q$-expansion principle (the variable $u$
corresponds to the grading).

nodes.name: Constant term morphism $q^0$
nodes.statement:
The morphism $q^0 :
{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}[[q]] \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ sending a  power series to its
constant term induces a ring morphism ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]] [u] \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u]
$.

nodes.name: Diagram for $q^0$ on holomorphic forms
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ L \ar[r] \ar[d]_{{\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}, u}}} & {MF} \ar[d] \\ {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u] & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u] . \ar[l]^{q^0} }
nodes.label: eqn:q0_hol

nodes.name: Tate curve formal group law reduces to $\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}}$
nodes.statement:
The composite $L \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u]$ classifies the  (graded) formal
group law  associated to the Tate Weierstrass curve defined
over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]] [u]$. After reduction $q \mapsto 0$, this is the
multiplicative (graded) formal group law ${\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}, u}}$ over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u]$, since the Tate curve has
multiplicative reduction.

nodes.name: Formal group law of the Weierstrass curve
nodes.statement: The universal Weierstrass curve over the ring of holomorphic modular forms ${MF}$ is not an elliptic curve; however, the associated formal group law is defined, since the curve is smooth at the identity section. Similarly for the Tate curve.

nodes.name: Meromorphic modular forms ${MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}$
nodes.statement:
The ring ${MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}$ of  meromorphic modular forms over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ is isomorphic
to $ {MF} [\Delta^{-1}]$, where $\Delta$ is the discriminant.

nodes.name: Diagram for $q^0$ on meromorphic forms
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ L \ar[r] \ar[d]_{{\mathbb{G}_{\mathrm{m}, u}}} & {MF} \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[d] & {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \ar[d] \\ {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}] & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][u] \ar@{^(->}[r] \ar[l]^{q^0} & {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [[q]][q^{-1},u^{\pm 1}], \ar@{-->}@/^2pc/[ll]^{q^0} }
nodes.label: eqn:mf-fgl

nodes.name: Elliptic homology ${Ell}$
nodes.statement:
The morphisms $L \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}] $ and $L \rightarrow
{MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}$ are Landweber exact and correspond respectively to
$KU_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ (which will be denoted here simply by $KU$) and a version of elliptic homology, denoted  by  ${Ell}$.
nodes.statement_short: $KU$ and elliptic homology ${Ell}$ are the Landweber exact theories from $L\to\mathbb{Z}[1/6][u^{\pm1}]$ and $L\to MF^{\mathrm{mer}}$.

nodes.name: ${Ell}_0KU$ is Katz's ring of divided congruences
nodes.statement: \cite[Theorem 2.7]{laures}. The ring ${Ell} _ 0 KU$ is isomorphic to Katz's ring $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ of divided congruences over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$.
conclusions:
The ring ${Ell} _ 0 KU$ is isomorphic to Katz's  ring
$\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ of divided congruences over ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$.

nodes.name: Structure of ${Ell}_*KU$
nodes.statement: \ \begin{enumerate} \item The ring ${Ell}_* KU $ is concentrated in even degree and is $2$-periodic. \item The ring ${Ell}_0 KU$ is a subring of ${Ell}_0 KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}\cong ({Ell}_* \otimes KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q})_0$ and identifies with the sub-${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$-module of sums $\sum_i f_i $ of modular forms such that the Fourier expansion $\Sigma_i f_i(q)$ has coefficients in ${\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$; this is precisely the ring $\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ of divided congruences \cite{katz}. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Miller's elliptic character realizes $q^0$
nodes.statement:
The additive morphism $q^0 : {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \rightarrow {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [u^{\pm 1}]$ is
realized by a morphism of spectra $q^0 : {Ell} \rightarrow KU$, which is
derived from Miller's elliptic character (see
\cite{laures}, following Miller \cite{millerW}).

nodes.name: Reduction map $\overline{\rho}^1$
nodes.statement:
Hence there is an induced
morphism of spectra
$
{Ell} \wedge {Ell}
\rightarrow
KU \wedge {Ell} ,
$
which induces a morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules
\[
\overline{\rho}^1 : {Ell}_* {Ell}
\rightarrow
KU_* {Ell},
\]
which is used in defining Laures' $f$-invariant \cite{laures}  (see Section \ref{subsect:f_inv}).

nodes.name: Rational Künneth for ${Ell}$ and $KU$
nodes.statement:
Since  ${Ell}$ and $KU$ are Landweber exact,  ${Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong
{Ell}_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and $KU_* {Ell} \otimes
\mathbb{Q} \cong  KU_*\otimes {Ell}_*  \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: Rationalization of $\overline{\rho}^1$
nodes.statement: The morphism $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is the morphism of right ${Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$-modules: \[ q^0 \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} : {Ell}_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \rightarrow KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} \cong KU_* \otimes {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q} \]
nodes.statement_short: $\overline\rho^1\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ is $q^0\otimes{Ell}_*\otimes\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.label: prop:rho_rat

nodes.name: Short exact sequences for $\overline{\rho}^1$
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \ \ \ \ 0 \ar[r] & {Ell}_*{Ell} \ar[r] \ar[d]_{\overline{\rho}^1} & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] \ar[d]^{\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}} & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \ar[r] \ar[d]^{\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} & 0 \\ 0 \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell} \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar[r] & KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \ar[r] & 0. }
nodes.label: eqn:ses-rho1

nodes.name: $\overline\rho^1\otimes\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ determined by $q^0$
nodes.statement:
Thus  $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ is determined by $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ and
hence by the additive morphism $q^0$.

nodes.name: Choice of $\overline\rho^1$ versus $\rho^1$
nodes.statement: Following \cite[Theorem 4.2]{behrens_laures}, the morphism $\overline{\rho}^1$ is used here to define the $f$-invariant rather than the analogous morphism $\rho^1 : {Ell}_*{Ell} \rightarrow {Ell}_* KU$ (compare \cite[Proposition 3.9]{laures}). The relationship between the two approaches to calculating the $f$-invariant is explained by \cite[Proposition 3.10]{laures}.

nodes.name: Cocycle $\kappa_{Ell}$
nodes.statement:
Base change along $MU_* \rightarrow {Ell}_*$ gives a cocycle
\[
\kappa_{{Ell}} :=\  _{{Ell}_*}\kappa _{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{{Ell}_*}
({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) ,
{Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]),
\]
which represents a class $[\kappa_{{Ell}}] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1 _{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0), {Ell}_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}}[-4])$,
by Lemma \ref{lem:cocycle-base-change}.

nodes.name: $\kappa_{Ell}$ is the reduction of $_{Ell_*}K_{Ell_*}$
nodes.statement: The morphism $\kappa_{{Ell}}$ is the reduction of the morphism \[ _{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom}_{{Ell}_*} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]) \] via the morphism ${Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \twoheadrightarrow {Ell}_* {Ell}\otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]$.
nodes.label: lem:kappa_ell_Xi

nodes.name: $\overline\rho^1$ applied to $\kappa_{Ell}$
nodes.statement: The morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[ (\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \circ \kappa_{Ell} \in \mathrm{Hom} ({Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]) \] coincides with the morphism $_{KU_*} \kappa _{{Ell}_*}$. Hence, the morphism $(\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} ) \circ \kappa_{Ell}$ is the reduction of the morphism of right ${Ell}_*$-modules \[_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*} \in \mathrm{Hom} ({Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]) \] via the morphism $KU_* {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \twoheadrightarrow KU_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} [-4]$.
nodes.statement_short: $(\overline\rho^1\otimes\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z})\circ\kappa_{Ell}={}_{KU_*}\kappa_{Ell_*}$, the reduction of ${}_{KU_*}K_{Ell_*}$.
nodes.label: prop:kappa-tmf

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.7
nodes.statement: The diagram of short exact sequences (\ref{eqn:ses-rho1}) together with Lemma \ref{lem:kappa_ell_Xi} show that it is sufficient to calculate the respective morphisms to $KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}$. This can be carried out using the identification of $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ given by Proposition \ref{prop:rho_rat}. There is a commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) \ar@/^1pc/[rd]^{_{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*}} \ar[d]_{_{{MF}}K_{{Ell}_*}} \\ {MF} \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \ar[d]_{q^0 \otimes {Ell}_*} \ar[r] & {Ell}_* \otimes _{MU_*} MU_* {Ell}_*\otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4] \ar@/^1pc/[ld]^(.4){\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}} \\ KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4], } \] where the horizontal morphism is induced by ${MF} \rightarrow {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \cong {Ell}_*$. The commutativity of the top triangle follows from the fact that the elliptic formal group law is defined over the ring of holomorphic modular forms, ${MF}$, and the commutativity of the lower triangle follows from the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:mf-fgl}). To complete the proof, observe that the vertical composite is the morphism $_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*}$, by the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:q0_hol}).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to rational targets and chase a diagram through holomorphic modular forms and $q^0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to rational
nodes.statement:
The diagram of short exact sequences (\ref{eqn:ses-rho1}) together
with Lemma \ref{lem:kappa_ell_Xi} show that it is sufficient to calculate the
respective morphisms to $KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}$. This can be carried out
using the identification of $\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ given by Proposition \ref{prop:rho_rat}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the rational morphisms via Proposition 6.4.

nodes.name: Diagram via MF
nodes.statement:
There is a commutative diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
{Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)
\ar@/^1pc/[rd]^{_{{Ell}_*}K_{{Ell}_*}}
\ar[d]_{_{{MF}}K_{{Ell}_*}}
\\
{MF} \otimes_{MU_*} MU_*{Ell}  \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4]
\ar[d]_{q^0 \otimes {Ell}_*}
\ar[r]
&
{Ell}_* \otimes _{MU_*} MU_* {Ell}_*\otimes
\mathbb{Q} [-4]
\ar@/^1pc/[ld]^(.4){\overline{\rho}^1 \otimes \mathbb{Q}}
\\
KU_* {Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} [-4],
}
\]
where the horizontal morphism is induced by ${MF} \rightarrow  {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}} \cong {Ell}_*$.
The commutativity of the top triangle follows from the fact that the
elliptic formal  group law  is defined over the ring of holomorphic modular forms, ${MF}$, and the commutativity of
the lower triangle follows from the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:mf-fgl}).
nodes.statement_short: Diagram through $MF$ commutes since the elliptic FGL is defined over $MF$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
To complete the proof, observe that the vertical composite is the morphism $_{KU_*}K_{{Ell}_*}$, by the
commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:q0_hol}).
nodes.statement_short: Vertical composite is ${}_{KU_*}K_{Ell_*}$.

nodes.name: $f$-invariant
nodes.statement:
The $f$-invariant of Laures  \cite{laures} is a
homomorphism
\[
f :
\pi_{2k}(S) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}
\rightarrow
\mathfrak{D} _\mathbb{Q} / \Big( \mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} + ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q} +
({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{k+1})_\mathbb{Q} \Big).
\]

nodes.name: Invariant $\iota^2$
nodes.statement:
This factorizes across an invariant
\[
\iota^2 : 	\mathrm{Ext}^{2,2k+2} _{MU_*MU} (MU_* , MU_*) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}
\hookrightarrow
\mathfrak{D} _\mathbb{Q} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q} \oplus
({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{k+1})_\mathbb{Q} \Big),
\]
where the injectivity is given by \cite[Proposition 3.9]{laures}.

nodes.name: Cobar complex $M_k^{\bullet+1}$
nodes.statement:
Write $M_k ^{\bullet +1} \cong \pi_{2k} ({Ell}^{\bullet +1})$ for the cobar complex associated to
${Ell}$.

nodes.name: Behrens-Laures semi-cosimplicial morphism
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ M_k^{(1)} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|{d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|{d_1} \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^0} & M_k^{(2)} \ar@<1ex>[rr]|{d_0} \ar@<0ex>[rr]|{d_1} \ar@<-1ex>[rr]|{d_2} \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^1} && M_k^{(3)} \ar[d] \ar[d] _{\overline{\rho}^2} \\ ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \ar@<.5ex>[r]|(.6){d_0} \ar@<-.5ex>[r]|(.6){d_1} & \mathfrak{D}_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \ar@<1ex>[rr]|(.3){d_0} \ar@<0ex>[rr]|(.3){d_1} \ar@<-1ex>[rr]|(.3){d_2} && \mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q} / \big( ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q} \big) }
nodes.label: eqn:BL_semicosimplicial

nodes.name: $\iota^2$ via $\overline{\rho}^2$
nodes.statement:
The composite of $\overline{\rho}^2$ with the projection
\[
\mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q} / \big(
({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}}
\oplus
({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q}
\big)
\twoheadrightarrow
\mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q} / \big(
\mathfrak{D}_{{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_k)_{\mathbb{Q}} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q}
\big)
\]
induces the morphism
\[
\iota^2 : 	\mathrm{Ext}^{2,2k} _{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_*) \otimes {\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}
\hookrightarrow
\mathfrak{D} _\mathbb{Q} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q} \oplus
({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{k})_\mathbb{Q} \Big),
\]
on restriction to cocycles.

nodes.name: Cobar differentials $\delta^i$
$\iota^2$ via $\overline{\rho}^1$
nodes.statement: Let $x$ be a $2$-cocycle in $M_k^{(2)}$ which represents a class $$[x] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{2, *} _{{Ell}_* {Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*).$$ Then \begin{enumerate} \item there exists an element $c \in M_k^{(1)}$ and an integer $n$ such that $\delta^1 c = nx$; \item the invariant $\iota^2 [x]$ is represented by the element $\frac{1}{n}\overline{\rho}^1 (c) \in \mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $x$ be a $2$-cocycle in $M_k^{(2)}$ which represents a class $$[x] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{2, *} _{{Ell}_* {Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*).$$
conclusions: there exists an element $c \in M_k^{(1)}$ and an integer $n$ such that $\delta^1 c = nx$
the invariant $\iota^2 [x]$ is represented by the element $\frac{1}{n}\overline{\rho}^1 (c) \in \mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}$
nodes.label: lem:iota2_rho1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement: A straightforward consequence of the commutative diagram (\ref{eqn:BL_semicosimplicial}) together with the fact that $\mathrm{Ext}^d_{{Ell}_*{Ell}}({Ell}_* , {Ell}_*) \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is trivial for $d >0$.
nodes.statement_short: Diagram (12) plus rational vanishing of positive Ext.

nodes.name: $f$-invariant of a chromatic 1-cocycle
nodes.statement: Let $[c] \in \mathrm{Ext}^{1,2k}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]})$ be represented by a cocycle $c : {Ell}_* [2k] \rightarrow {Ell}_* {Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}$ which factorizes as left ${Ell}_*$-module morphisms \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_*[2k] \ar[r]^(.4){\hat{c}} \ar[rd] _c & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q} \ar@{->>}[d] \\ & {Ell}_*{Ell} \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]}. } \] Then the invariant $\iota^2( \partial_1 [c])$ is represented by the image of the generator under the map \[ \xymatrix{ {Ell}_*[2k] \ar[rr]^(.45){\ _{KU_*} \hat{c} _{{Ell}_*} } && KU_*{Ell} \otimes \mathbb{Q}, } \] where $KU_{2k} {Ell}\otimes \mathbb{Q}$ is identified with $\mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}$ by periodicity.
nodes.statement_short: If $c$ lifts rationally to $\hat c$, then $\iota^2(\partial_1[c])$ is represented by ${}_{KU_*}\hat c_{Ell_*}$ of the generator in $\mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.label: prop:f-inv_1cocycle

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 7.2
nodes.statement: The result follows from Lemma \ref{lem:iota2_rho1}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Lemma 7.1.

nodes.name: $f(\mathfrak{p})$
nodes.statement: For $\mathfrak{p}$ a primitive in $\mathbf{P} MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$, let $f(\mathfrak{p})$ denote the $f$-invariant of $ \mathfrak{p}^* [\kappa]\in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{MU_*MU} (MU_*[|\mathfrak{p}| +4] , MU_* \otimes {\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]})$.

nodes.name: Reduced Bernoulli numbers $\overline{B}_n^{Ell}$, $\overline{B}_n^{KU}$
nodes.statement:
For $n$ a natural number, write $\overline{B}_n ^{{Ell}}\in {Ell}_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ (respectively
$\overline{B}_n ^{KU} \in KU_* \otimes \mathbb{Q}$) for the reduced Bernoulli numbers associated to the complex
orientations of ${Ell}$ and $KU$ respectively.

nodes.name: $\overline{B}_n^{Ell}$ is a holomorphic modular form
nodes.statement: The reduced Bernoulli number $\overline{B}_n ^{{Ell}}$ is defined in the ring ${MF} \otimes \mathbb{Q}$ of holomorphic modular forms, since the formal group law of ${Ell}_*$ is the image of a formal group law over ${MF}$ via the morphism ${MF}\hookrightarrow {MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}\cong {Ell}_*$.

nodes.name: $f$-invariant on primitives $p_s\otimes p_t$
nodes.statement: Let $s,t$ be natural numbers. The $f$-invariant $$f(p_s \otimes p_t) \in \mathfrak{D} _\mathbb{Q} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_\mathbb{Q} \Big),$$ is represented by the element $ - \overline{B}_{t+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU} \in \mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}. $
nodes.statement_short: $f(p_s\otimes p_t)$ is represented by $-\overline B^{Ell}_{t+1}\overline B^{KU}_{s+1}$.
nodes.label: thm:f-pspt

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.5
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:f-inv_1cocycle}, these invariants are represented by the morphism $ \ _{KU_*} ( K \circ \mathfrak{p}) _{{Ell}_*}. $ Hence, by Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim}, $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by \[ (\overline{B}_{s+1} ^{{Ell}} - \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU}) \overline{B}_{t+1}^{{Ell}} \in \mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}. \] The term $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{{Ell}} \overline{B}_{t+1} ^{{Ell}}$ becomes zero on passage to the quotient, since it belongs to the subgroup $({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 7.2 plus Proposition 5.8; the $\overline B^{Ell}\overline B^{Ell}$ term is a modular form and vanishes in the quotient.

nodes.name: Apply Prop 7.2
nodes.statement:
By Proposition \ref{prop:f-inv_1cocycle}, these invariants are represented by the morphism
$
\ _{KU_*} ( K \circ \mathfrak{p}) _{{Ell}_*}.
$
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 7.2 reduces to ${}_{KU_*}(K\circ\mathfrak p)_{Ell_*}$.

nodes.name: Apply Prop 5.8
nodes.statement:
Hence, by  Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim},
$f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by
\[
(\overline{B}_{s+1} ^{{Ell}} - \overline{B} _{s+1} ^{KU}) \overline{B}_{t+1}^{{Ell}}
\in
\mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 5.8 gives the representative.

nodes.name: Quotient
nodes.statement:
The term $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{{Ell}} \overline{B}_{t+1} ^{{Ell}}$ becomes zero on passage to the quotient, since it belongs to
the subgroup $({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: Drop the modular-form term in the quotient.

nodes.name: Symmetric form of the $f$-invariant
nodes.statement: Let $s,t$ be natural numbers. The invariant $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ is represented by the element $ \overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU} \in \mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}. $
nodes.statement_short: $f(p_s\otimes p_t)$ is represented by $\overline B^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}$.
nodes.label: cor:symm_f-invariant

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 7.6
nodes.statement: The group $\mathfrak{S}_2$ acts on $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ by comodule morphisms induced by interchanging the factors $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0$. It is straightforward to show that the induced right action on $\mathrm{Ext}_{MU_*MU} ^2 (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , MU_* [-4]) $ satisfies \[ ([e_\tau]^2 ) \sigma = \mathrm{sgn} (\sigma) [e_\tau]^2. \] Hence $ f (p_s \otimes p_t) = - f (p_t \otimes p_s); $ in particular, the $f$-invariant of $p_s \otimes p_t$ is represented by the element $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU}$.
nodes.statement_short: Antisymmetry of $[e_\tau]^2$ under swapping factors gives $f(p_s\otimes p_t)=-f(p_t\otimes p_s)$.

nodes.name: Sign action
nodes.statement:
The group $\mathfrak{S}_2$ acts on $MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)$ by comodule morphisms induced by interchanging the factors $\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0$. It is straightforward to show that the induced right action on $\mathrm{Ext}_{MU_*MU} ^2 (MU_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) , MU_* [-4]) $ satisfies
\[
([e_\tau]^2 ) \sigma = \mathrm{sgn} (\sigma) [e_\tau]^2.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Swap action; $[e_\tau]^2$ transforms by the sign.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Hence
$
f (p_s \otimes p_t) = - f (p_t \otimes p_s);
$
in particular, the $f$-invariant of $p_s \otimes p_t$ is  represented by the element $\overline{B}_{s+1}^{Ell} \overline{B} _{t+1} ^{KU}$.
nodes.statement_short: Antisymmetry gives the formula.

nodes.name: $f'$-invariant
nodes.statement:
For $p \geq 5$ a prime, Behrens \cite{behrens} defines the $f'$-invariant via a morphism
\[
f' :
\mathrm{Ext}^{2,2k+2} _{MU_*MU} (MU_* , MU_*)_{(p)}
\rightarrow
H^0(C (l)^\bullet/p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty )_{2k+2},
\]
where $l$ is a topological generator of $\mathbb{Z}_p^\times$ (for example $l = \gamma$) and $C(l)^\bullet$ is an
explicit semi-cosimplicial abelian group which is defined in terms of modular forms of level one and modular forms of level $l$.

nodes.name: Modular forms $M_k(\Gamma_0(l))_{\mathbb{Z}_p}$
nodes.statement:
Namely, as in \cite{behrens}, write $M_k (\Gamma_0 (l))_{\mathbb{Z}_p}$ for the space of modular forms of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(l)$  over $\mathbb{Z}_p$
which are meromorphic at the cusps.

nodes.name: Semi-cosimplicial group $C(l)^\bullet$
$BP$ and $p$-typical orientation conventions
nodes.statement: Behrens and Laures work $p$-locally and replace $MU$ by $BP$, so as to accord better with the results of Miller, Ravenel and Wilson \cite{MRW}. Thus, below ${Ell}_*$ denotes $p$-local elliptic homology ($p \geq 5$), and a $p$-typical orientation $BP_* \rightarrow {Ell}_*$ is fixed, as in \cite{behrens_laures}.

nodes.name: Behrens-Laures diagram for the $f'$-invariant
nodes.statement_short: The $f'$-invariant factors through $\partial_1\partial_2$, $L_{v_2}$ and the isomorphism $\tilde\eta$.

nodes.name: Diagram for the $f'$-invariant
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \mathrm{Ext}^{2,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*) \ar[dd]_{f'} & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty) \ar[l]_{\partial_1\partial_2} \ar[d]^{L_{v_2}} \ar@/_1pc/[ldd] \\ &\mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_*BP} (BP_*, BP_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty [v_2^{-1}]) \ar[d]^\cong \\ H^0(C (l)^\bullet/p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty )_{4t} & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty), \ar[l]^(.55){\cong}_(.55){\tilde{\eta}} }
nodes.label: eqn:f'_invariant

nodes.name: Algebraic double transfer via $BP_*(\overline\Theta)$
nodes.statement:
Recall that $\overline{\Theta}$ defines a chromatic factorization of the double transfer and this
induces a commutative diagram
\begin{eqnarray} \xymatrix{
&
\mathrm{Ext}_{BP_*BP}^{0,*-4} (BP_* , BP_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0))
\ar[d]^{BP_* (\overline{\Theta})}
\ar[ld]
\\
\mathrm{Ext}^{2,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_*)
&
\mathrm{Ext}^{0,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_* /p^\infty, v_1^\infty)
\ar[l]^{\partial_1 \partial_2},
}
\end{eqnarray}
by Proposition \ref{prop:kappa-transfer} and Proposition \ref{prop:second-factorization} (with  $BP$ in place of $MU$).

nodes.name: Diagram for the algebraic double transfer
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ & \mathrm{Ext}_{BP_*BP}^{0,*-4} (BP_* , BP_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)) \ar[d]^{BP_* (\overline{\Theta})} \ar[ld] \\ \mathrm{Ext}^{2,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_*) & \mathrm{Ext}^{0,*}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_* /p^\infty, v_1^\infty) \ar[l]^{\partial_1 \partial_2}, }
nodes.label: eqn:alg_double_transfer

nodes.name: Independence of the choice of $\overline\Theta$
nodes.statement: The composite morphism \[ \xymatrix{ \mathrm{Ext}_{BP_*BP}^{0,4t -4} (BP_* , BP_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) ) \ar[rr]^{BP_* (\overline{\Theta})} && \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{BP_* BP} (BP_* , BP_* /p^\infty, v_1^\infty) \ar[d] \\ && \mathrm{Ext}^{0,4t}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}} ({Ell}_*, {Ell}_*/p^\infty,v_1^\infty) } \] induced by the change of rings associated to the $p$-typical orientation $BP_* \rightarrow {Ell}_*$, is independent of the choice of $\overline{\Theta}$.
conclusions: is independent of the choice of $\overline{\Theta}$
nodes.label: lem:independence_Theta

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.8
nodes.statement: Follows from the commutativity of the diagrams (\ref{eqn:f'_invariant}) and (\ref{eqn:alg_double_transfer}), together with the fact that the bottom horizontal morphism in (\ref{eqn:f'_invariant}) is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Diagrams (13), (14) and the isomorphism $\tilde\eta$.

nodes.name: $f'$ invariant for primitive elements
nodes.statement:
By naturality, it suffices to replace the composite morphism considered above by the morphism
\[
{Ell}_* (\overline{\Theta}) :
\mathrm{Ext}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}}^{0,4t -4} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) )
\rightarrow
\mathrm{Ext}_{{Ell}_*{Ell}}^{0,4t} ({Ell}_* , {Ell}_* /p^\infty,v_1^\infty )
\]
which is considered as being the $f'$ invariant for primitive elements.

nodes.name: Diagram for $f'$ and $f''$
nodes.statement:
Theorem \ref{thm:MU-thetas} gives a commutative
diagram
\[
\xymatrix{
&
\mathbf{P} {Ell}_*(\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)
\ar@{^(.>}[d]
\ar@/^1pc/@<4em>@{.>}[dd]^{f'}
\ar@/^3pc/@<4em>@{.>}[ddd]^{f''}
\\
{Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_{-1} \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)
\ar[dd]_{{Ell}_* (\theta)}
&
{Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0 \wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0)
\ar@{.>}[l]_{\sigma'}
\ar[d]^{{Ell}_*(\overline{\Theta})}
\\
&
{Ell}_* /p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty [-4]
\ar@{^(->}[d]
\\
{Ell}_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}[-4]
\ar[r]
&
{Ell}_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}/\Big({Ell}_*KU _{(p)} \oplus ({Ell}_*)_\mathbb{Q} \Big) [-4],
}
\]
where the solid arrows denote comodule morphisms and the dotted arrows morphisms of
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-modules.

nodes.name: $f''$
nodes.statement:
The composite of $f'$ with the monomorphism ${Ell}_* /p^\infty, v_1 ^\infty [-4]
\hookrightarrow {Ell}_* KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}/\Big({Ell}_*KU _{(p)} \oplus ({Ell}_*)_\mathbb{Q} \Big) [-4]$ is denoted $f''$, as indicated.

nodes.name: Integrality of ${Ell}_*(\theta)$
nodes.statement: The morphism ${Ell}_* (\theta)$ composed with the morphism induced by $\psi^\gamma - 1$ is integral in the appropriate sense, as a consequence of the construction of $\theta$. This can be related to the analysis of $H^0 (C(l)^\bullet/ p^\infty, v_1^\infty) $ using the identifications of \cite[Proposition 6.1]{behrens}.

nodes.name: Formula for ${Ell}_*(\theta)\circ\sigma'$
nodes.statement:
The morphism ${Ell}_*(\theta) \circ \sigma'$ is given by Proposition
\ref{prop:MUtheta_sigmap}, after base change  to ${Ell}_*$; it is determined by $
\underline{\beta}_0 (x) \otimes \underline{\beta}_0 (y)
\mapsto $
\[
\Big( \frac{1}{\underline{b}'(x) } - \frac{1}{x}\Big)
\Big(\frac{1}{\log^{{Ell}} y} - \frac{1}{\underline{b}' (y) }\Big)
+
\sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!}
\left(
\frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1}
\right)
(\log^{Ell} x)^{i-1}(\log ^{Ell} y) ^{j-1},
\]
where the power series $\underline{b}'$ is understood as $\exp^{KU} \circ
\log^{Ell}$ when considered as a power series over ${Ell}_* KU  \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.

nodes.name: $f'$-invariant on primitives
nodes.statement: The $f'$-invariant on the primitives of ${Ell}_* (\mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0\wedge \mathbb{C} \mathbf{P}^\infty_0) $ is determined by \[ f'' (p_s \otimes p_t) = \Big[ \overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} + \overline{B}^{KU}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1}\frac{\gamma^{s+1}(1- \gamma^{t+1}) }{\gamma^{s+t+2}-1} \Big], \] where $s, t$ are natural numbers and $ \overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} + \overline{B}^{KU}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1}\frac{\gamma^{s+1}(1- \gamma^{t+1}) }{\gamma^{s+t+2}-1} $ is considered as an element of ${Ell}_*KU \otimes \mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.statement_short: $f''(p_s\otimes p_t)=[\overline B^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}+\overline B^{KU}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}\gamma^{s+1}(1-\gamma^{t+1})/(\gamma^{s+t+2}-1)]$.
nodes.label: thm:fprime

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.10
nodes.statement: The method of proof is similar to that used in Proposition \ref{prop:restrict_Xi_prim}. Substitute $x= \exp^{Ell} S$ and $y = \exp^{Ell} T$ in the power series representing ${Ell}_* (\theta) \circ \sigma'$; this gives the power series \[ \Big( \frac{1}{\exp^{KU} S} - \frac{1}{\exp^{Ell} S }\Big) \Big(\frac{1}{T} - \frac{1}{\exp^{KU} T }\Big) + \sum _{i, j >0}\frac{B_i^{KU}}{i!}\frac{B_j^{KU}}{j!} \left( \frac{\gamma^i -1}{\gamma^{i+j}-1} \right) S^{i-1}T ^{j-1}. \] The result follows by identifying coefficients.

nodes.name: Relation between $f$ and $f'$ on primitives
nodes.statement: The relationship between the $f$ and the $f'$ invariants (in the general case) is made explicit in \cite[Theorem 4.2]{behrens_laures} by analysing the semi-cosimplicial diagram (\ref{eqn:BL_semicosimplicial}). Upon restricting to classes arising from comodule primitives via the algebraic double transfer, the relationship is clear. Observe that Theorem \ref{thm:f-pspt}, Corollary \ref{cor:symm_f-invariant} and Theorem \ref{thm:fprime} show that, on passage to the quotient $$\mathfrak{D} _\mathbb{Q} / \Big(\mathfrak{D}_{\mathbb{Z}[{\scriptstyle{\frac{1}{6}}}]} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_0)_\mathbb{Q} \oplus ({MF}^{\mathrm{mer}}_{s+t+2})_\mathbb{Q} \Big)$$ the elements $f(p_s \otimes p_t)$ and $f'(p_s \otimes p_t)$ both are defined by the class of the element $\overline{B}^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline{B}^{KU} _{t+1} $ in $\mathfrak{D}_\mathbb{Q}$, since the additional term appearing in Theorem \ref{thm:fprime} becomes trivial in this quotient. The relationship can be seen as a direct consequence of Lemma \ref{lem:restrict_Theta} and Corollary \ref{cor:relate_MUtheta}; here, the sign appearing in the leading term in Corollary \ref{cor:relate_MUtheta} has been avoided by following Behrens and Lawson in defining the $f$-invariant by using the morphism $\overline{\rho}^1$.
nodes.statement_short: On double-transfer classes from primitives, $f$ and $f'$ agree in the quotient, both given by $\overline B^{Ell}_{s+1}\overline B^{KU}_{t+1}$.
nodes.label: rem:relate_f,f'

nodes.name: Comodule notation $\Gamma$-Comod, $\psi_M$
nodes.statement: For $(A,\Gamma)$  a Hopf algebroid, the category of left $\Gamma$-comodules is denoted here $\Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$ and the category of $A$-modules  $A\hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod}$; the structure morphism of a $\Gamma$-comodule $M$ is written $\psi_M : M \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A M$.
nodes.section: A Cohomology and cocycles for Hopf algebroids

nodes.name: Flat Hopf algebroid $(A,\Gamma)$
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, $(A,\Gamma)$ is a flat Hopf algebroid, so that $\Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$ is abelian with enough injectives; extension groups in this category are denoted by $\mathrm{Ext}_\Gamma$;  the extended comodule functor $\Gamma \otimes _A - : A\hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod} \rightarrow \Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$ is right adjoint to the forgetful functor $\Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod} \rightarrow A \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod}$.

nodes.name: Unreduced cobar resolution
nodes.statement:
For $M$  a $\Gamma$-comodule, let $(\tilde{D}_\Gamma ^\bullet M, d^\bullet)$
denote  the unreduced cobar resolution of $M$ (Cf. \cite[Definition A1.2.11]{ravenel_green}).

nodes.name: $A$-projective and relatively injective comodules
nodes.statement: \ \begin{enumerate} \item A $\Gamma$-comodule $X$ is $A$-projective if its underlying $A$-module is projective. \item A $\Gamma$-comodule $J$ is relatively injective if it has the morphism extension problem with respect to monomorphisms of $\Gamma$-comodules which are split as $A$-module morphisms. \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Characterization of relatively injective comodules
nodes.statement: A $\Gamma$-comodule $J$ is relatively injective if and only if it is a direct summand of an extended comodule.
conclusions: relatively injective if and only if it is a direct summand of an extended comodule

nodes.name: Ext into extended comodules
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule and $N$ an $A$-module. Then there is a natural isomorphism \[ \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma (M, \Gamma \otimes _A N ) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^i _A (M, N) . \] Hence, if $X$ is an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $J$ is a relatively injective $\Gamma$-comodule, \[ \mathrm{Ext}^i _\Gamma(X, J) = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, J) & i= 0 \\ 0 & i >0. \end{array} \right. \]
nodes.label: lem:ext_vanishing

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.3
nodes.statement: The result follows from the argument of \cite[Lemma A1.2.8b)]{ravenel_green}.
nodes.statement_short: Argument of Ravenel, Lemma A1.2.8(b).

nodes.name: Ext via relatively injective resolutions and the cobar complex
nodes.statement: \cite[Lemma A.1.1.6, Corollary A1.2.12]{ravenel_green} Let $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule. Then $ \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_\Gamma (X, M)$ can be calculated by a resolution of $M$ of the from $M \rightarrow J^\bullet$, where each $J^k$ is relatively injective. In particular, $ \mathrm{Ext}^\bullet_\Gamma (X, M)$ is naturally isomorphic to the cohomology of the cocomplex $\mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, \tilde{D}^\bullet_\Gamma M)$, which has terms $\mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma^{\otimes_A s }\otimes _A M)$.
nodes.label: prop:ext-cobar

nodes.name: 1-cocycle representatives
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and $M$ be a $\Gamma$-comodule. An extension class $[\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1 _\Gamma (X, M)$ is represented by a cocycle $\kappa \in \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A M )$.
conclusions:
is represented by a cocycle
$\kappa \in
\mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A M )$
nodes.label: cor:1-cocycle

nodes.name: First cobar differential $d^0$
nodes.statement: Let $X, M$ be as in Proposition \ref{prop:ext-cobar} and let $\alpha : M \rightarrow N$ be a morphism of $\Gamma$-comodules. \begin{enumerate} \item The differential $d^0_M : \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, M) \rightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A M )$ is given by $ d^0_M g := (\Gamma \otimes g ) \circ \psi_X - \psi_M \circ g. $ \item The differential $d^0_N : \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, N) \rightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A N )$ satisfies the relation $ d^0_N (\alpha \circ g) = (\Gamma \otimes _A \alpha) \circ d^0_M g. $ \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $d^0_Mg=(\Gamma\otimes g)\circ\psi_X-\psi_M\circ g$, natural in $M$.
nodes.label: lem:d0

nodes.name: Explicit connecting morphism
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be an $A$-projective $\Gamma$-comodule and \[ 0 \rightarrow N_1 \rightarrow N_2 \rightarrow N_3 \rightarrow 0 \] be a short exact sequence of $\Gamma$-comodules. For a morphism of $\Gamma$-comodules $h : X \rightarrow N_3$ and any lift $\tilde{h}: X\rightarrow N_2$ of $h$ as a morphism of $A$-modules: \begin{enumerate} \item the morphism $\Delta \tilde{h}:= (\Gamma \otimes \tilde{h}) \circ \psi_X - \psi_{N_2} \circ \tilde{h}$ lies in the image of $\mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A N_1 ) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Hom}_A (X, \Gamma \otimes_A N_2)$; \item the morphism $\Delta \tilde{h} : X \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A N_1$ is a cocycle and the associated class in $\mathrm{Ext}^1 _\Gamma (X, N_1)$ satisfies $[\Delta \tilde{h}] = \partial h$, where $\partial : \mathrm{Hom}_\Gamma (X, N_3) \rightarrow \mathrm{Ext}^1_\Gamma (X, N_1)$ is the connecting morphism. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For a module lift $\tilde h$ of $h:X\to N_3$, $\Delta\tilde h$ is a cocycle into $\Gamma\otimes N_1$ representing $\partial h$.
nodes.label: lem:explicit-connecting

nodes.name: Cocycle from a module splitting
nodes.statement: Let \begin{eqnarray} 0 \rightarrow M \rightarrow \mathcal{E} \stackrel{p}{\rightarrow} X \rightarrow 0 \end{eqnarray} be a short exact sequence of $\Gamma$-comodules, in which $X$ is $A$-projective. Then, for any choice of section $\sigma : X \rightarrow \mathcal{E}$, with associated retract $r :\mathcal{E}\rightarrow M$, the composite: \[ X \stackrel{- \sigma}{\rightarrow} \mathcal{E} \stackrel{\psi_{\mathcal{E}}}{\rightarrow} \Gamma \otimes _A \mathcal{E} \stackrel{\Gamma \otimes r}{\rightarrow} \Gamma \otimes_A M \] is a cocycle which represents the extension class $\partial 1_X$, which corresponds to the short exact sequence (\ref{eqn:ses-comod}). A different choice of splitting as $A$-modules gives rise to a cohomologous cocycle.
nodes.statement_short: For a SES of comodules with section $\sigma$ and retract $r$, $-(\Gamma\otimes r)\psi\sigma$ represents the extension class.
nodes.label: prop:cocycle-canonical-splitting

nodes.name: Short exact sequence of comodules
nodes.statement: 0 \rightarrow M \rightarrow \mathcal{E} \stackrel{p}{\rightarrow} X \rightarrow 0
nodes.label: eqn:ses-comod

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition A.8
nodes.statement: Consider the cocycle given by Lemma \ref{lem:explicit-connecting}, where $h$ is taken to be the identity morphism of $X$ and $\tilde{h}$ the section $\sigma$. Then the morphism $\Delta \tilde{h}$ is the difference $(\Gamma \otimes \sigma) \circ \psi_X - \psi_{\mathcal{E}} \circ \sigma$, considered (by abuse of notation) also as a morphism to the image of $\Gamma \otimes_A M$ in $\Gamma \otimes_A \mathcal{E}$. Hence, composing with the retraction $\Gamma \otimes r$ gives $\Delta \tilde{h}=(\Gamma \otimes r) \Delta \tilde{h}$; now $r \circ \sigma =0$, so that $\Delta \tilde{h} = -( \Gamma \otimes r) \circ \psi _{\mathcal{E}} \circ \sigma$, as required. The final statement is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma A.7 with $h=1_X$, $\tilde h=\sigma$ and use $r\circ\sigma=0$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma A.7
nodes.statement:
Consider the cocycle given by Lemma \ref{lem:explicit-connecting}, where $h$ is taken
to be the identity morphism of $X$ and $\tilde{h}$ the section $\sigma$. Then the
morphism $\Delta \tilde{h}$ is the difference $(\Gamma \otimes \sigma) \circ \psi_X - \psi_{\mathcal{E}} \circ \sigma$, considered (by abuse of notation)
also as a morphism to the image of $\Gamma \otimes_A M$ in $\Gamma \otimes_A \mathcal{E}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma A.7 with $h=1_X$, $\tilde h=\sigma$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, composing with the retraction $\Gamma \otimes r$ gives $\Delta \tilde{h}=(\Gamma \otimes r) \Delta \tilde{h}$; now $r \circ \sigma =0$,  so that $\Delta \tilde{h} = -( \Gamma \otimes r) \circ \psi _{\mathcal{E}} \circ \sigma$, as required. The final statement is clear.
nodes.statement_short: Use $r\circ\sigma=0$ to get the formula.

nodes.name: Base change setting
nodes.statement:
Let $(A, \Gamma)$ be a flat Hopf algebroid and let $B
\stackrel{b}{\leftarrow} A \stackrel{c}{\rightarrow }C$ be ring morphisms.
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness

nodes.name: Rings ${_B\Gamma_C}$
nodes.statement: Write ${_B\Gamma_C}$ for the ring $B \otimes _A \Gamma \otimes _A C$ and $\Gamma_B$ (respectively $\Gamma_C$) for the ring $ _B\Gamma_B$ (resp. $_C \Gamma _C$).
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness

nodes.name: Induced Hopf algebroids
nodes.statement: There are induced Hopf algebroids $(B, \Gamma_B)$ and $(C, \Gamma_C)$.
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness

nodes.name: Bicomodule structure on ${_B\Gamma_C}$
nodes.statement:
The ring $_B\Gamma_C$ has a left  $(B,\Gamma_B)$- right $(C,
\Gamma_C)$-bicomodule structure and the structure morphisms are
algebra morphisms.
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness

nodes.name: Landweber exact morphism
nodes.statement: \cite{HS_comod} A morphism $b : A \rightarrow B$ is Landweber exact with respect to $(A,\Gamma)$ if the functor $B\otimes_A - : \Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod} \rightarrow B \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Mod}$ is exact.
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness
nodes.label: def:Landweber_exact

nodes.name: Landweber exact base change
nodes.statement: \cite{HS_comod} If $b : A \rightarrow B$ is Landweber exact with respect to $(A, \Gamma)$, then $(B, \Gamma_B)$ is a flat Hopf algebroid and $B \otimes_A -$ induces an exact functor $B\otimes_A - : \Gamma \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod} \rightarrow \Gamma_B \hspace{-.2em}-\hspace{-.2em} \mathrm{Comod}$.
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness
assumptions: $b : A  \rightarrow B$ is Landweber exact with respect to $(A, \Gamma)$

nodes.name: Base-changed morphism $_Bf_C$
nodes.statement: For $f: X \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A M $ a morphism of left $A$-modules, write $_Bf_C : B \otimes _A X \rightarrow {_B\Gamma_C} \otimes _A M$ for the morphism of left $B$-modules: \[ B \otimes _A X \stackrel{B \otimes f } {\rightarrow} B \otimes _A \Gamma \otimes _A M \stackrel{B \otimes A \otimes c \otimes M}{\rightarrow} {_B\Gamma_C} \otimes _A M. \]
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness

nodes.name: Base change of a cocycle
nodes.statement: Let $X, M$ be as in Proposition \ref{prop:ext-cobar}; a cocycle $\kappa : X \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A M$ induces a morphism $_B \kappa _C : B\otimes_A X \rightarrow {_B\Gamma_C} \otimes _A M \cong {_B\Gamma_C} \otimes_C (C \otimes_A M)$.
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness

nodes.name: Naturality of base change
nodes.statement: Let $f : X \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes_A M $ and $g: M \rightarrow N$ be morphisms of left $A$-modules. There is an identity \[ _B ((\Gamma \otimes_A g) \circ f ) _C = \Big( {_B\Gamma_C} \otimes_C (C \otimes_A g) \Big) \circ \ _Bf_C. \]
nodes.section: A.2 Base change and Landweber exactness
nodes.label: lem:cocycle_base_change

nodes.name: Base change of cocycles
nodes.statement: Let $A\stackrel{b}{\rightarrow} B$ be a Landweber exact morphism for $(A,\Gamma)$ and $X,M$ be $\Gamma$-comodules such that $X$ is $A$-projective. Let $\kappa : X \rightarrow \Gamma \otimes _A M$ be a cocycle representing an extension $[\kappa] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1_\Gamma (X, M)$. Then $B \otimes_A X$ is a $B$-projective $\Gamma_B$-comodule and the morphism $_B\kappa_B : B \otimes _A X \rightarrow \Gamma _B \otimes _B (B \otimes _A M) $ is a cocycle which represents the class $B \otimes _A [\kappa ] \in \mathrm{Ext}^1_{\Gamma_B} (B \otimes_A X , B \otimes_A M)$.
